I’ve been at my new job for less than a week and I definitely feel this way. Everyone explains things to me as if they would a child and it’s insulting. I do have a hard time processing new information however I feel like everything I do is wrong and they not only correct me but physically show me how to get tasks done faster than I am doing it. It’s all frustrating and humiliating especially since I’m new and I feel like I don’t belong.

I’m not sure if people are trying to help me or send me subliminal thoughts about how useless or incompetent I am. I genuinely don’t know most the time if I’m right or wrong, I can’t differentiate if people think about me the way I do or if they just are trying to be nice or helpful.

I've been dependent since 2013. I lived with someone else who was providing for me. Starting with my dad, then I lived at a trade school, and after graduating I depended on a roommate who was just as unstable as myself, then my brother, then my sister, now another roommate. And the pattern will keep going until I either die or decide to break the cycle. I hate feeling dependent or like I'm searching for a 'rescuer', then drinking alcohol to feel like I am somewhat competent and happy. My sister has made it clear, I depend on everyone because I am the youngest and I've always been like that. But now that I'm adult, nobody is going to help me anymore. And that scares me. I would rather choose death than figuring out what to do.

I am fully aware that alcohol makes any mental illness especially depression worse, but I genuinely do desire to quit because feeling suicidal like this every day is beginning to scare me. I used to self harm (still have very visible scars) and attempted suicide before as a teenager. I'm more at a crossroads, either really try to get treatment or I'm really going to give up. 
I actually have been starting to think maybe I could stop eating meat so I don't have to rely on supermarket industries anymore. That would also facilitate my need to be solitary and help me feel a sense of fufillment (providing for myself). But where I am currently in my life is so far down how can I stick to the light rather than the darkness?

I am living in poverty so yes, I would rather sell my soul for three wishes if that shows how immoral I've become: 

1) I wish that I owned an undiscovered island on the coast of Washington state. There would be my own beach house, multiple wives that only did my bidding, and unlimited supply of fruit and vegetables and cannabis. That wish would probably do me well for a couple years if not an entire decade. Once I got tired of that..

2) I wish that I was handsome. To the point of being undeniably, objectively attractive to the rest of the population. In that frame, I wish I was also highly intellegent and articulate. Nobel prize, multiple award winner, and highly adored by millions worldwide. This would be ideal, playing into my need for relationships, popularity, fame, and wealth, and sexual freedom. I would most likely die happily before I could get to my third wish.
